description: React components for transactional emails, email templates, landing pages, invoices, reports and PDFs. Render email-safe HTML, responsive web HTML and print-ready PDF HTML from one component tree.
rules: Install @unlayer/react-elements. The root must be <Email>, <Page> or <Document> (use Document for print/PDF).
Structure is Root > Row > Column > content (Button, Paragraph, Heading, Image, Divider, Menu, Social, Html, Table, Video). Content components do not nest.
A Row's layout must match its number of Column children, e.g. ColumnLayouts.TwoEqual needs exactly 2 Columns.
renderToHtml() returns a complete HTML document; renderToJson() returns Unlayer design JSON that the Unlayer editor opens with loadDesign(). Both are synchronous.
There is no Text component: use Paragraph for body text and Heading for headings.
Start with packages/react/docs/README.md for task selection. Runnable transactional email, provider, PDF, and visual editing recipes are in packages/react/docs/ and examples/content-workflows/.
Elements renders HTML, not email delivery or PDF bytes. Send email HTML through a provider; print Document HTML with Playwright Chromium for a real PDF.
For shared templates, pass a factory result with an actual Email/Page/Document root to renderers. Keep Row and Column nodes directly visible to renderToJson.
renderToJson statically walks supported Elements nodes, not arbitrary React components. Edited design JSON does not regenerate JSX; use editor.exportHtml for edited HTML.

To move React Email templates to Elements, run `npx @unlayer/migrate <folder> --report migration.md`, read the report, then add `--write`. It keeps props, loops and conditions, checks every template against the original, and lists what differs. After converting a template by hand, check it with `npx @unlayer/migrate compare <original> <migrated>`. See packages/react/docs/migrate-from-react-email.md.
To open React Email templates in the Unlayer editor, run `npx @unlayer/migrate <folder> --out <dir> --design` and pass each `<name>.design.json` to `loadDesign()`. See examples/react-email-in-editor.
